programme.title: The Flood 1: First Pulse
programme.desc: The Okavango Delta is a water phenomenon on the sands of the Kalahari Desert.Every year, heavy rains transform the barren region into a true oasis teeming with life.In a two-part documentary, director Brad Bestelink introduced the inhabitants of this unique place on Earth.The camera lens included both small dragonflies and giant elephants.Spectacular photos were taken from various perspectives - from the ground, from a bird's eye view and from the water depths.Scenes of exciting hunting intertwine with the idyll of life in a fertile land.Masters of survival The story begins while waiting for rain.On a sun-baked, dry and barren land, there is a fight for survival.Wild cats - a cheetah and a leopard - show off their skills.She stands out for her speed, he is able to lure his prey into an ambush.They both turn out to be effective in hunting, for example, impala.As the rain pours down, the region undergoes an almost magical transformation.The water attracts herds of various animals.Among them are African buffalos, which are hunted by lions.Viewers will also learn about the adventures of a longclaw who tries alone to ensure the safety of three chicks.Scenes from the lives of various species form a story about a complex ecosystem.

programme.title: One Strange Rock
programme.desc: A story about the creation and history of the planet, the laws governing it, its shape, the richness of flora and fauna, threats to the natural environment, natural wonders and surprising relationships.Actor Will Smith and people who have had the opportunity to spend time in space will talk about this extraordinary place in the universe.Accounts from astronauts including Mae Jemison, Mike Massimino, Leland Melvin and Chris Austin Hadfield will provide a completely new perspective on Earth.Director Darren Aronofsky and his film crew visited 45 countries and six continents.The photos were taken in, among others, the Arctic, the Himalayas, India and during the annual festival in Tarragona, Spain.Materials recorded on board the International Space Station were also used.In the following episodes, viewers will learn how oxygen is produced, the protective layers of the Blue Planet and the entire sequence of events that led to the creation of life.The topic of death, colonization, destruction, the search for alien forms and human intellect will also be discussed.

programme.title: Big Cat Planet
programme.desc: Big cats, symbols of wild nature, today face the challenge of survival in a changing world.More and more often, their paths cross with people, leading to inevitable conflicts.On this journey, we learn about their unique adaptive skills: cheetahs use cars for hunting, jaguars dive near boats, and lions appear more and more often on the streets of Indian cities.This fresh look shows the cunning of predators that are still among the most dangerous inhabitants of nature.

programme.title: Animal fights
programme.desc: Unique shots of spectacular clashes involving the largest and most dangerous predators on our planet.This extraordinary series also features animals that, although seemingly gentle, are surprisingly belligerent when threatened.We will see how brave they are, among others.lions, wolves, hippos and crocodiles.We will see to what extent the result of the duel depends on strength and weapons such as teeth or claws, and to what extent it depends on good tactics.The program used materials recorded by the best nature photographers, as well as films made by amateurs who witnessed fierce fights in the animal world.

programme.title: Animal Genius
programme.desc: Biologist Liz Bonnin has been revealing the secrets of the fauna kingdom for years.In this film, he observes animals that are very good at fighting predators, even though they do not have sharp claws and fangs.Their survival is related to skills such as communication and cooperation.It turns out that nature still hides many secrets from us.The observed animals surprise scientists who make new discoveries.This time they will learn patents for survival, including:in Africa and Mexico.There is strength in a herd. Charming meerkats have already been the heroines of many documentaries and TV series.Curious mammals living in the Kalahari Desert are exposed to attacks by predators.They can inform each other about various threats.Their characteristic sound signals are crucial.Viewers will also watch the battle between Matabele warrior ants and termites.Unusual insects can provide first aid to injured companions.In Mexico, Liz Bonnin will observe sea turtles.The small reptiles face a dangerous journey to the ocean.They move towards the water together, increasing their chances of survival.These scenes show that in nature, it is not only the strongest who survive, but also the best connected.
